boundaries.label: LOCAL HOST · application + managed bridge + private storage

cards.title: 01 · Primary path
items: Highlighted route: signed-in user runs Check Now → shared processor → selected WhatsApp adapter → bridge → WhatsApp network.
The processor fetches product data before evaluating the alert. Creation saves a tracker; it does not send immediately.
Eligible = condition met, active, inside the time window, and not fully notified. Channels follow the owner's preference.
Evidence: DashboardController.cs:135–142; PriceTrackingProcessor.cs:48–286; WhatsAppWebNotificationService.cs:170–239.

cards.title: 02 · Runtime & scheduling
items: Web, worker, processor, scraper and adapters are logical modules in one .NET 8 process. They are not separate network services.
A five-second scan finds due trackers; per-tracker intervals and Asia/Karachi schedule windows control eligibility. Manual and scheduled checks share a lock.
WhatsAppBridgeWorker starts/restarts Node, or reuses an existing authenticated bridge. The bridge owns headless Chromium.
Evidence: Program.cs:9–44; PriceTrackingServices.cs (PriceTrackingWorker); TrackingSchedule.cs; WhatsAppBridgeWorker.cs:8–94.

cards.title: 03 · External paths
items: Retailer path: server-side HTTP(S) fetch → HTML / product JSON parsing → price and stock result. Shopify selects the requested variant; HTTP 429 delays that host.
Email uses the configured SMTP server; SSL/TLS defaults on but is configurable. WhatsApp uses whatsapp-web.js, not the official Business API.
In-app alerts stay in SQLite; the browser polls /Notifications/Recent every 25 seconds. This supporting path is kept off the edge map.
Evidence: PriceTrackingServices.cs:29–140; ShopifyProductScraping.cs; EmailNotificationService.cs:10–47; notifications.js:150–151.

cards.title: 04 · Trust boundaries
items: Browser → app: cookie identity is revalidated against stored accounts; owner filters protect trackers; admin role gates SMTP and sender controls; modifying forms use antiforgery.
App → bridge: loopback-only address, bearer secret, Host/Origin checks, and no redirect following. The browser receives no bridge secret.
Remote content and user URLs are untrusted. URL validation accepts HTTP(S); no private-address or DNS destination filtering was found in the inspected scraper path.
Private storage depends on host filesystem permissions. SQLite and persisted SMTP settings are not encrypted by this code. Chromium is launched with --no-sandbox.
Evidence: AccountCookieEvents.cs; SqliteTrackingStore.cs:40–74; http-server.js:5–30; ProductUrlAttribute.cs; ISmtpConfigurationStore.cs; server.js:47–65.

cards.title: 05 · State & delivery semantics
items: SQLite stores users, trackers, in-app alerts, SMTP settings and per-channel receipts; bridge token, linked session and send journal live separately in .local/whatsapp.
Successful channels are recorded individually. Later checks retry missing channels; a tracker is fully notified only after every selected channel succeeds.
The bridge journals a stable alert reference before sending. An ambiguous send blocks automatic resubmission for that reference; submission does not prove delivery or reading.
Evidence: SqliteDatabase.cs:30–60; SqliteTrackingStore.cs:95–150; InAppNotificationService.cs; PriceTrackingProcessor.cs:163–286; sender.js:14–103.

cards.title: 06 · Scope & evidence limits
items: 12 core components / 12 relationships. This map describes the inspected working copy and default single-host arrangement, not an observed production deployment.

No Git metadata is present in this checkout: citations are local source references, not commit-verified provenance. Full paths and file hashes are in analysis.md and source-manifest.json beside this diagram.
Signup verification is a development logger registered in Program.cs, separate from real alert delivery. No reverse proxy, hosted queue, or distributed scheduler is evidenced here.
Evidence: Program.cs:18, 36–37; AccountServices.cs (DevelopmentWhatsAppVerificationService); DATABASE_SETUP.md; WHATSAPP_SETUP.md.
